title: theHarvester against radblok.co.za
summary: Ran theHarvester against my own domain radblok.co.za. Hit the google source error again (removed in 4.11.1 — same as Entry 005). Documented the correct free sources for a .co.za domain and what to realistically expect from a small 2-year-old site.

sections.h: Attempt 2: google source — same error as Entry 005

blocks.label: kali

blocks.text: Google scraping was removed from theHarvester 4.11.1 entirely — Google actively blocks it. This is the same error hit in Entry 005 against microsoft.com. **The `-b google` habit doesn't work in this version.** Use `crtsh`, `dnsdumpster`, `hackertarget` or other sources instead.

sections.h: Correct approach: working sources for a .co.za domain

blocks.text: For `radblok.co.za` — a small, 2-year-old domain registered with xneelo — the most realistic free sources are:

head: Source
What it searches
Needs API key?
rows: Certificate Transparency logs — every TLS cert ever issued for the domain
Passive DNS — historical records from DNS crawls
Pages scanned by urlscan.io that reference the domain
AlienVault OTX — threat intelligence, passive DNS

blocks.label: kali — crtsh (best first try, no API needed)
kali — save results to file
blocks.text:
$ theHarvester -d radblok.co.za -l 500 -b crtsh,dnsdumpster -f radblok_harvest
# Writes radblok_harvest.json and radblok_harvest.xml

For a large domain (microsoft.com, github.com) crtsh has thousands of CT log entries. For a small personal domain like `radblok.co.za` with one or two certs ever issued, results will be thin — that's expected, not a tool failure.

sections.h: What to realistically expect from radblok.co.za

blocks.text: radblok.co.za was registered 2024-04-09 and is 2 years old with xneelo hosting. Realistic expectations per source:

head: Source
Expected result
rows: One or two certs (wildcard `*.radblok.co.za` or bare domain). Fewer certs than github.com by orders of magnitude.
May show the A record and nameservers — same info as whois/dig, just from a different angle.
Similar — passive DNS from crawls, likely just the main A record.
Only shows results if the domain was previously submitted or crawled by urlscan.io. Could be empty.
Threat intel — will likely return nothing for a clean personal domain.

blocks.text: A thin result is not a bug. theHarvester is built for recon against targets that have significant public footprint. Against your own small domain it confirms what you already know from whois and dig — useful for verifying the tool works and understanding what each source actually queries.

The crtsh 502 issue from Entry 005 (wildcard query against huge domains failing silently as 'no hosts found') is less likely for a small domain — crtsh handles small exact-match queries reliably. If you see 'No hosts found' on `radblok.co.za`, it likely means no CT logs exist yet, not a crtsh failure.

items: Confirmed `-b google` is still broken in 4.11.1 — same as Entry 005, not version-specific to this run.
Documented the full theHarvester flag reference from the usage output.
Identified correct free sources for a .co.za domain: `crtsh`, `dnsdumpster`, `hackertarget`, `urlscan`, `otx`.
